decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up left approach to the cars; plan white basket for cars, center for cameras, red for watches. Initial lift and gradual downward wrist rotation.
Advance above the left car with open gripper, progressively pointing the fingers down while preserving the elbow-up branch.
Fine-align over the left car, rotate the jaw line across its width and descend slowly. Wrist view will determine final grasp correction.
Use wrist-image alignment: car remains ahead of the pinch line. Shift toward it while maintaining a slow, shallow approach and open jaws.
Center the car between the fingers, lower two centimeters and close gently. Grasp retention remains to be checked by lifting.
Lift the closed gripper to check car retention before transporting toward the white basket.
The car remained on the table. Reopen and correct the approach toward its visually projected center rather than continuing the failed grasp.
Correct using wrist displacement: move the car down toward the pinch line and lower while keeping the jaws open. Camera-based alignment is more reliable here than the head depth estimate.
Center the visible car at the pinch line, close, and perform a short test lift. Avoid further descent against the observed tracking resistance.
The test lift did not retain the car. Reopen, correct its lateral offset in the wrist image, and lower incrementally to bring fingers alongside the small car.
At the lower height the car is behind the pinch line. Translate toward it in the wrist-image down direction, close, and check contact with a small lift.
Maintain closure and lift the car clear of the table; begin moving toward the white basket only after vertical clearance. Verify retention from the next views.
Car visibly retained. Carry it over the white basket with the gripper commanded closed, then begin a shallow lowering for release.
Replan after the rejected forward step: lower first and tilt fingers slightly forward to reach inside the white basket without extending the arm further at the high pose.
The first car is now visible inside the white basket. Open and withdraw toward the remaining car, keeping the left arm on its side.
Lower toward the second car with jaws open, correcting its rightward wrist-image offset before closure.
Second car is centered across the jaws. Descend a little to its sides, close completely, and begin a short retention test.
Lift with closure maintained to verify the second car is retained; start a short leftward transit at clearance height.
Second car is visibly retained. Move left into the white basket approach, lowering slightly and pitching forward to keep a safe reach margin.
The held car contacted the basket front rim. Replan from the observed pose: lift clear and tilt forward, avoiding further forward extension until it clears.
The second car slipped outside the white basket. Reopen and approach it again from the front, staying clear of the basket rim.
Align the upside-down car with the pinch line using its wrist-image offset, lowering in small increments before reclosing.
Back away from the basket-wall contact and restore a more vertical pinch, then close around the car in front of the rim for a small test lift.
Lift the regrasped car well clear of the rim while retreating slightly. A forward wrist pitch will let the car enter the basket without pushing the elbow toward full reach.
With the car held above rim height, move its center over the white basket interior and release without dragging across the front wall.
Allow the car to drop and settle, then withdraw toward the left camera. Keep open jaws and regain a downward approach for the camera category.
Both cars are visible in white. Align the left camera across its narrow dimension using the wrist view, descending with open fingers.
Camera is now aligned lengthwise. Correct its remaining right/down offset in the wrist view, close across its sides, and start a small test lift.
Lift the left camera to verify retention and clear the table before moving centrally. Begin a gradual elbow-up approach with the right arm for the other camera.
Left camera slipped onto the table. Reopen and reacquire at its new location, while bringing the right gripper above the right camera with a downward approach.
Use both wrist views to align across the cameras' narrow dimensions. Make small lateral corrections and descend with open grippers, keeping each arm in its own workspace.
Finish small wrist-based centering corrections, lower alongside both camera bodies, and close. Use a short lift to test retention before transport.
Lift both closed grippers while retreating from the basket rims. Check camera retention visually before choosing the next transport or regrasp.
Right camera is retained; carry it toward the blue basket on the right side of center. Left camera stayed on the table, so reopen and correct toward its body before another grasp.
Bring the right camera over the blue basket. For the flat left camera, align more centrally and lower the fingers beside its thin body before closing.
Release the retained right camera over the blue interior and withdraw. Lift the left camera away from the rim with closure maintained to verify the new grasp.
Right camera is in blue; approach the rightmost watch. Left camera was not retained, so reapproach from farther in front with a forward-tilted pinch to avoid the white rim.
Correct the left camera's up-left wrist offset and close around its body with a short test lift. Lower the right gripper toward the watch, leaving it open for visual alignment.
The left pinch still appears above the flat camera, so reopen and lower beside it. Correct the right watch toward the pinch line, close both, and test minimally.
Both objects now appear between the finger sides. Lift vertically with closure maintained, retreating slightly from the white rim, and inspect retention before any basket transit.

Left camera is visibly retained; carry it across the front toward blue, staying left of center. The right watch remained on the table; reopen and correct toward its lower wrist-image position while descending.
Bring the retained left camera over the left half of blue while maintaining rim clearance. Close around the right watch at the lower, centered approach and lift to verify retention.
Release the second camera into blue and withdraw left toward the remaining watches. Carry the visibly retained right watch toward red at rim-clearing height with a gradual forward wrist pitch.
Release the first watch into red, then withdraw the right arm toward the center watch. Left descends toward the remaining silver watch to reposition it for a non-crossing transfer.
Center and close the left gripper on the silver watch. Approach the green watch with the right EE kept on its own side, tilting its fingers slightly toward center.
Test the silver-watch grasp while moving the left gripper away from the center to create clearance. Right makes a small wrist-based correction and descends toward the green watch.
Silver watch was not retained; reopen and approach farther toward its body. Right closes on the centered green watch and begins a clearance lift away from the left gripper.

Both watches remain on the table. Correct the silver watch's wrist offset and close at a lower height. Reopen the right gripper and lower further so its fingers reach the green watch's sides rather than closing above the band.
Give the central grippers more clearance. Align the green watch laterally at its lower approach, close, and lift it toward the right while keeping the left gripper open.
The green watch appears retained; raise it clear and carry toward red. Correct the silver watch toward the pinch line and grasp at a lower height, followed by a short lift check.
Carry the retained green watch over red and release. The silver watch remained on the table, so reopen, lower beside its band, and close at the lower grasp height.
Allow the green watch to settle in red. Move the left pinch slightly toward the silver watch's center, clear table pressure, close and lift; right withdraws to prepare for a center-side pickup.
Silver watch is now visibly retained. Set it down near the centerline, still on the left side, for pickup by the inward-tilted right gripper after the left arm withdraws.
Withdraw the open left gripper fully from the transfer area before the right approaches. The right EE remains positive-x while its inward-tilted fingers approach the silver watch.
Lower the right fingers toward the transferred watch with the EE remaining right of center. Return the empty left arm toward its origin gradually, maintaining configuration continuity.
Fine-align the right pinch with the transferred silver watch, close at the lower height, and test lift. Finish the left arm's gradual return toward origin.
The silver watch is between the finger sides. Lift to confirm retention and carry toward red at clearance height, while the left arm remains at origin.
Silver watch is visibly retained. Carry it over the red basket with closure maintained and a slight forward pitch, keeping it above the rim.
Release the final watch into red, allow it to fall, then withdraw the open right gripper away from the rim and start a continuous return toward origin.
All three watches are visible in red, cameras in blue and cars in white. Continue the open right arm's gradual return toward origin while leaving the baskets undisturbed.
